windowTitle: Serial integration stage 11.5 - Fabric Secret binding replacement and the second model configuration

necessity.decision: docs/decisions.md#2026-10-01-fabric-owns-explicit-secret-binding-replacement keeps FabricCoordination.BindSecret as initial-bind and same-request replay only and adds FabricCoordination.RebindSecret with expected predecessor CAS and provider confirmation; docs/spec/target/06_data_flow_and_state_machine.md F09 rows 5 and 5a split the first bind from the replacement; row 8 revokes the predecessor Gateway key only after Serve readback.
necessity.currentProblem: fabric.secret_bindings is UNIQUE on (execution_resource_id, purpose) WHERE revoked_at IS NULL and no code wrote revoked_at, so a second model configuration for the same runtime slot replayed the first binding; the Workspace then handed Serve a stale Secret generation that the real execution boundary refused. The production contract had no replacement operation, so the second configuration could not be implemented without fabricating success, weakening the uniqueness invariant, or revoking the old key before the new runtime was confirmed.
confirmedFacts: docs/decisions.md and docs/spec/target/contracts/internal.proto on the branch (44d754fe, merged 942ad18c) declare SecretBindingRebindCommand { expected_current_secret_binding_id, key_binding_id, secret_delivery_reference, target_slot, fingerprint } and SecretBindingRebindReadback { previous_secret_binding_id, secret_binding_id, ... } and rpc RebindSecret.
The production packages/contracts/proto/internal.proto did not carry those messages or the rpc before this pass.

The Workspace records the Fabric Secret binding id it confirmed in the update_models operation result (orderResult.SecretBindingID), so a later configuration can name the exact predecessor its own prior confirmation established.
Gateway Integration already admits the Fabric audience for BINDMANAGEDSECRET, so the Workspace->Fabric rebind authorization path was already in place.
necessity.outcome: The production internal.proto gained the SSOT RebindSecret messages and rpc and its Go bindings were regenerated with the pinned protoc-gen-go; Fabric implements predecessor CAS under the per-workspace lock, provider confirmation, predecessor retirement and replacement write in one transaction with an idempotent readback; Workspace binds initially when it has no predecessor and rebinds otherwise, then revokes the predecessor Gateway key only after Serve confirms the new applied version.

ssotConformance.requirement: BindSecret never silently replaces a different Secret; RebindSecret compares the expected predecessor, confirms the replacement through the provider, preserves one active binding and never revokes the Gateway key.
ssotConformance.conformance: BindSecret still refuses a different Secret with AlreadyExists; RebindSecret requires the exact active predecessor, retires it and writes the replacement in one transaction so the partial unique index never sees two active bindings, and the Fabric code never calls Gateway revocation.

ssotConformance.requirement: revoked_at means the Fabric binding is no longer active; the predecessor stays recoverable until Serve confirms the new model version and Gateway revokes the predecessor key.
ssotConformance.conformance: RebindSecret sets revoked_at on the predecessor and writes the replacement; nothing else writes revoked_at, and Gateway key revocation remains a separate Workspace action.

ssotConformance.requirement: A predecessor Gateway key remains valid until the replacement Secret and new Runtime model version are confirmed by Fabric and Serve; unknown replacement or compensation blocks subsequent side effects until readback.
ssotConformance.conformance: Workspace revokes the predecessor only after Serve reports the new applied version; a failed or mismatched replacement leaves the predecessor key live and the applied version unchanged, proven by focused tests.

focused.covers: RebindSecret predecessor CAS, provider confirmation, one-active-binding invariant, idempotent replay, wrong-predecessor refusal, idempotency conflict, foreign-peer refusal and denied authorization; plus the existing BindSecret initial-bind/replay/conflict test.

the first configuration binds initially, the second configuration rebinds against the exact recorded predecessor, Serve carries the replacement generation, the applied version advances only from Serve readback, the predecessor key is revoked only after confirmation, a mismatched rebind readback is refused before Serve, a failed rebind keeps the predecessor key and leaves the outcome unknown, plus the existing update/replay/tenant/selection tests.
Serve still consumes the opaque RuntimeManagedKeyBinding and mints nothing on the reload path.
the Workspace accepted-operation grant still admits the Fabric audience for BINDMANAGEDSECRET.
deterministic regeneration of the internal bindings including RebindSecret; no publicjson drift.
